claims.claim: A tort is an act or omission that causes injury or harm and amounts to a civil wrong for which courts impose liability.
Tort law generally aims to provide relief for harm, impose liability on responsible parties, and deter harmful conduct.
Introductory tort law commonly distinguishes intentional, negligent, and strict-liability torts.
Strict-liability torts do not depend on the degree of care used in the same way as intentional and negligent torts.
Tort remedies commonly include monetary damages, and an injunction may be available in some cases.
Compensatory damages address losses, while punitive damages may be awarded under applicable law to punish or deter particularly blameworthy conduct.
Tort law is distinct from criminal law and contract law, although the same conduct can sometimes create both tort and criminal questions.
